startup_seconds.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). The runs read 1.016, 0.904 and 0.891 s, the medians of their three launches (2.027, 1.016, 0.932; 1.986, 0.904, 0.759; 2.216, 0.886, 0.891 s), the first of each paying for a cold page cache. Against 0.69 s in September, on Arch's qt6-webengine 6.11.2-1, that is 0.2 s later, with the runs within 0.13 s of each other. The ceiling is about four times the old median, which is what the startup probes in docs/development.md use, because a shared runner's speed is not its own. It moved towards its ceiling by more than the runs' spread (0.13 s): 23% of the ceiling became 30%. Most of that is the runner, not the browser (#883): 0.69 s was one run, and September's 54 main runs read a median of 0.945 s (0.64 to 1.02 s). The processor a runner draws moves the number between 0.5 and 0.9 s, and two of these three runs drew the EPYC 7763, the slowest. On that processor alone, startup went from 0.77 s on 2026-10-06 to 0.92 s: Qt 6.12 about 30 ms, the Omarchy kit sync (4757651, #729) 34 to 48 ms, and the CRT glass's halation (3f47e4b, #785) 36 ms, both between engine-started and window-mapped. The engine's update is none of it: one build read 0.921 s on 6.11.2-16 and 0.923 s on 6.11.3-1. #883 took the halation's share back, 0.923 to 0.875 s on the EPYC 7763, because a Start page closed before the first frame no longer fades over it.

startup_lived_in_seconds.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). Process start to the first buffer on the toplevel's surface with the lived-in profile, file-cache cold, median of three launches. The profile is #618's reader's shape at about its size, 403 MiB: two Spaces, three open tabs, closed and put-away tabs, 106 visits, both filter lists, an 83 MiB extension and the engine's HTTP cache, Cache Storage and IndexedDB; the page cache is dropped before each launch. The runs read 1.606, 2.823 and 1.624 s, the medians of their three launches. The second landed on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, the other two on an AMD EPYC 7763 (1.6 s in all six launches), so the median is the EPYC's. The ceiling is about four times the median, as the startup ceiling is, because a shared runner's speed is not its own.

memory_mebibytes.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). Proportional set size of the whole process tree, one Space, one page: 504.4, 500.0 and 495.0 MiB at the first Space of the spaces step, and 502.51, 500.21 and 502.49 MiB in the memory step, the median of which is recorded. Against 481.45 MiB, recorded on 2026-09-15 in the shared arch-linux job on Arch's qt6-webengine 6.11.2-1 and Qt 6.11.2 rather than on Omaweb's engine, that is 21 MiB more (#884). The browser's own process grew: the renderer held, the zygotes shrank, and this runner starts no GPU or utility process. Read by #884's probe, which reads about 30 MiB above this step, the browser process held 366 to 371 MiB with September's tree and packages and 399 to 406 with today's. The engine's 6.11.3 update is not it: 6.11.2-16 reads the same. Omaweb's code since 2026-09-28 adds about 50 MiB to that process and Omaweb's engine holds about 30 less than Arch's, which leaves the 21. About 30 of the 50 came by 2026-10-08, after a step of 58 MiB with the Start page's Omnibar over the night road, its pictured rows and each Space's favicons (#460, #463, #465) that was mostly given back by 2026-10-03, and about 10 with the CRT glass (#785). heaptrack puts it in Qt Quick, in the objects, textures and layers the chrome makes as it starts, and turning off the Scene, the page blur or the tinting effects does not move it, so it is the cost of the chrome added since September and is kept. This is a Debug build: a release build reads about 90 MiB more and grew by about 80. This step's own split, on #884's run 40919000819: browser 373.5, renderer 74.8, zygotes 42.4 and session bus 1.7 MiB. The ceiling is twice the first recording, as the frozen-tab probe's is. It moved towards its ceiling by more than the runs' spread (2 MiB): 50% of the ceiling became 52%.

frozen_growth_mebibytes.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with #885's probe at d39ddab: the median of three readings in one budget-job run (run 40948225841). What an away Space's page goes on taking once frozen, over ten seconds, against ADR 0033. It is read from the processes that page started, by what they hold resident or swapped out, and from nothing else. The runs read 0.00, 0.00 and 0.00 MiB, and the same page grew 29.6 MiB in each of the six seconds it was on show. The probe read every engine process before #885, and recorded 0.44 MiB (0.58, 0.43 and 0.44) on the same engine at bcf3878b. None of that was the frozen page, whose renderer moved by 0 KiB and used no CPU in every probe. It was the page brought back on show: about twelve seconds after the switch, V8's memory reducer faults in 0.5 to 1 MiB of libQt6WebEngineCore and frees about 0.25 MiB, and --js-flags=--no-memory-reducer takes it to nothing. The step came with the first clang-built x86_64 engine (ADR 0060): main read 0.0 MiB up to 549d518 on 6.11.2-3 and 0.4 MiB from b2f37a6 on 6.11.2-5. With Freezing switched off, on a desktop, the page goes on at a timer tick a second and the probe reads 10.04 MiB. Tighter than the others on purpose: a page left running while away is throttled to a megabyte a second.

pageload_fresh_hosts_milliseconds.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). What Content blocking adds to a page of 40 images from 40 hosts it has never seen, the median with blocking on minus the median with the site switched off, ten loads each: 180.5 against 155.3 ms, 134.5 against 120.5 ms and 174.9 against 152.4 ms, so 25.2, 13.95 and 22.45 ms (18.2 ms on 6.11.2-3). The second run was on the Xeon. This holds CNAME uncloaking's lookups as well as the rule check, the Refusal tally and the refused-request list. Secure DNS off. The hosts resolve through dnsmasq on the container's resolver, with CNAME chains, not host-resolver rules. Procedural cosmetic filtering is measured separately under #402. The ceiling is four times the first recording's difference.

pageload_known_hosts_milliseconds.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). The same for 40 images from 4 hosts resolved on the warm-up loads: 182.4 against 179.5 ms, 159.3 against 153.2 ms and 179.2 against 181.8 ms, so 2.9, 6.1 and -2.6 ms (4.0 ms on 6.11.2-3). A difference this small is below what the runner can tell apart, which is why the third run came out negative. Four times the first recording's difference is 16 ms, under the 20 ms floor.

telemetry_background_cpu_percent.note: Re-recorded on 2026-10-29 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.3-1, with main at bcf3878b: the median of three budget-job runs (run 40869156387, attempts 1 to 3). What choosing the Telemetry Scene adds to the process tree's CPU while the reader is on a page, so no Start page draws: its sampler, which reads /proc and /sys four times a second so a new tab's graphs are full (#814). The tree's CPU over 30 s on a page with Telemetry chosen, less the same with no Scene, as a share of one core: 0.40 less 0.27, 0.33 less 0.20 and 0.43 less 0.30%, so 0.13% in all three. This is the first recording on CI's runner; the 0.37% it replaces was a laptop's, whose idle tree moved from 1.33 to 2.00% without Telemetry. Timed alone, a sample costs about 0.1 ms, 0.04% of a core at four a second. The ceiling is 2%, as the idle tree's is, because a difference this small moves with whatever else the machine is doing.
